name: Plan*RAG (Plan∗RAG): Efficient Test-Time Planning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop on Reasoning and Planning for Large Language Models (Reasoning and Planning for LLMs @ ICLR2025); preprint arXiv:2410.20753 (v1 Oct 2024, v2 Feb 2025)
authors_affiliation: Prakhar Verma (Aalto University; work during internship at Microsoft Research India), Sukruta Prakash Midigeshi, Gaurav Sinha, Nagarajan Natarajan, Amit Sharma (Microsoft Research India), Arno Solin (Aalto University)
code_url: [uncertain] No official public code repository was located (no GitHub link in the paper, on the authors' pages, OpenReview, or CatalyzeX as of the search date).
task_domain: Knowledge-intensive QA, specifically multi-hop (2-4 hop) and single-hop open-domain question answering over a Wikipedia corpus; framed as reasoning/planning over RAG.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, test-time inference setting. Given a multi-hop natural-language query and an external document corpus, the system must produce a grounded answer. No task-specific supervision is required at inference for the base method; a reasoning-plan generator can optionally be fine-tuned (LoRA on a small HotpotQA-train subset) but a capable LLM (GPT-4o) prompted zero-shot also works. The LM and retriever are frozen plug-and-play components; the only learned component is the optional plan generator.
what_is_retrieved: Documents (100-word Wikipedia passages/chunks) retrieved to ground the main query and/or each atomic sub-query in the reasoning DAG.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (2018 English Wikipedia, segmented into non-overlapping 100-word chunks, embedded with Contriever-MS MARCO). No agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: a fixed top-5 documents are retrieved per query (original query for the base variant, per atomic sub-query for the SubQ variant). The DAG decomposition aims to improve retrieval precision/recall through atomic sub-queries, but retrieval itself is fixed-k top-k, not a variable-size completeness recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is a test-time planning / structured-reasoning RAG method.
retrieval_unit: document (100-word Wikipedia passage/chunk); top-5 retrieved per query/sub-query.
index_source: Static corpus, constructed offline (2018 English Wikipedia embedded with Contriever-MS MARCO into a dense index). Not online/test-time-induced; the retrievable store is frozen.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over Wikipedia passage embeddings. (The DAG structure is over sub-queries/reasoning steps, not over the document index itself.)
retriever_type: Dense retriever (Contriever-MS MARCO, unsupervised contrastive dense embeddings).
retriever_learning_signal: None within Plan*RAG (off-the-shelf Contriever-MS MARCO used as-is). Contriever itself was pre-trained via unsupervised contrastive learning, but the retriever is not further trained or selected by Plan*RAG; retrieval improvement comes from better (atomic) query formulation, not retriever training.
query_construction: The main query is decomposed by an LLM into a DAG of atomic, dynamic sub-queries. Each sub-query is a node tagged with special placeholders <AI.J> referencing parent-node answers; at execution time these tags are dynamically instantiated with parent generations (e.g., 'In what year was <A2.1> published by Viking Press?' becomes 'In what year was The Outsiders published by Viking Press?'). Retrieval uses either the original query (base variant) or each instantiated atomic sub-query (SubQ variant).
query_granularity: Two-level / step-level: a task-level decomposition produced once at t=0 (the DAG plan), then per-node (atomic sub-query / step-level) query instantiation and retrieval as the DAG is traversed depth by depth.
when_to_retrieve: Plan-then-retrieve, then iterative along the DAG. Base Plan*RAG: one-shot retrieval on the original query reused for all nodes. Plan*RAG SubQ: iterative per-node retrieval (one retrieval per atomic sub-query) following the DAG topology. The decomposition plan is generated once (static template), instantiated dynamically during traversal.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule driven by DAG structure: retrieval is triggered per node when that node is reached during depth-ordered traversal (no learned router, no token-confidence or uncertainty trigger). The number/depth of retrievals is determined by the test-time-generated DAG, which adapts to query complexity (depth 0 for single-hop, deeper for multi-hop).
reranking: None. No reranking stage is reported; top-5 dense-retrieved documents are used directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose at the query level: complex queries are decomposed into atomic sub-queries so each retrieval is precise and only parent-node answers plus the node's own retrieved documents enter the context (selective information propagation / bounded context). No explicit document compression, distillation, or distractor-filtering module beyond this structural scoping.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools; documents indexed as raw 100-word Wikipedia chunks via Contriever embeddings).
index_content_separation: N/A (single flat document index; no separation of a lightweight index from heavy content). Note: the reasoning plan IS held outside the LM context as a global data structure, separating plan/control from per-node content, but this is at the reasoning-plan level, not the document index.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index, no live-sync protocol; static Wikipedia document index).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A for tools. Sub-query dependency awareness IS central: the DAG's directed edges explicitly encode conditional dependencies between sub-queries (output of parent node feeds child via <AI.J> tags); nodes at the same depth are conditionally independent and run in parallel.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: for each node q, the LLM is prompted with the (instantiated) sub-query q, its parent nodes' generated answers G(Pa(q)), and the documents D_q retrieved for q, to generate G(q). A final dataset-dependent aggregation operator Ω combines node generations into the final answer.
planning_integration: Plan-then-execute over an externalized DAG: the LLM first generates a full reasoning plan as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of atomic sub-queries at test time, decoupled from the LM context window; the DAG is then executed top-down (root to leaves), retrieving and answering per node, with parallel execution of same-depth nodes. Retrieve is interleaved at the sub-query/node level (retrieve-then-answer per node). Modular: the per-node solver can be a vanilla RAG step or another RAG method (e.g., Self-RAG), giving Plan*-Self-RAG.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per atomic sub-query (per DAG node). Each node corresponds to a single atomic reasoning step answerable by one retrieval; retrieval/answer is woven in per node rather than per CoT token or per single monolithic answer.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR case-adaptation method). The closest analog is dynamic instantiation of sub-query templates via <AI.J> tags using parent-node generations.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved Wikipedia passages injected into the prompt as context, alongside parent-node answer strings; the plan itself is a structured object (DAG / JSON of nodes and edges) held outside the LM context.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document passages (100-word Wikipedia chunks). The retrieved units are not distilled strategies, skills, or guidelines; abstraction/structure lives in the externalized reasoning DAG, not in the retrieved units.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Atomic, targeted sub-queries improve retrieval precision (Plan*RAGSubQ reaches 27.43 precision vs ~0.02-0.04 for ReAct/QD on HotpotQA distractor) and bounded per-node context (only parent answers + node documents) limits propagation of irrelevant context. The paper notes the DAG enables explicit per-node verification and backtracking, but states these are left to future work; no trained relevance evaluator or distractor-aware SFT is implemented.
memory_type: none (no persistent/episodic memory). The reasoning DAG is a per-query, transient global data structure, not a cross-query memory store.
write_back: False. No new experiences, cases, or skills are written back to any persistent store; the DAG is discarded after each query.
online_growth: False. The retrievable document store is frozen (offline-induced Wikipedia index); it does not grow at test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a persistent memory).
failure_experience_usage: N/A. No storage of successful or failed experiences. The DAG structure is said to facilitate per-node error isolation, backtracking, and re-decomposition, but these verification/intervention capabilities are explicitly left to future work and not used to store failures.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored entries to mutate). Within a single query, the static plan template is dynamically instantiated (tags filled with parent answers) during traversal, but nothing persists across queries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. Retrieval/sub-query selection is not an RL- or value-learned policy; it follows fixed top-k dense retrieval driven by the LLM-generated DAG. The optional fine-tuned plan generator is trained by supervised LoRA on (question, DAG-JSON) pairs, not by RL on retrieval outcomes.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No cross-agent memory sharing. However, the method is framework-agnostic / modular: the per-node solver can be swapped to other RAG frameworks (Self-RAG integration -> Plan*-Self-RAG), so Plan*RAG composes with heterogeneous RAG methods even though there is no shared experience memory.
benchmarks: HotpotQA (dev-fullwiki, 7,405 queries; also HotpotQA distractor setting for retrieval precision/recall and a 1,300-sample dev subset for planner comparison), StrategyQA (2,234 QA pairs, via Self-RAG repo), MuSiQue-Ans (2,417 questions, 2-4 hops), PopQA (1,399 QA pairs, single-hop).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, StrategyQA, MuSiQue) plus single-hop QA (PopQA). Open-domain Wikipedia QA.
baselines: Vanilla-LLM (no retrieval), Vanilla-RAG, CoT-RAG (chain-of-thought + retrieval), QD-RAG (query decomposition + retrieval, incl. QD-RAGSubQ), ReAct, Self-RAG, RQ-RAG. Base LLMs: GPT-3.5-turbo, Llama2-chat-13B, Llama3.1-instruct-8B (and Llama2-7B/13B for Self-RAG/RQ-RAG comparisons). Noted to have outperformed SAIL, Toolformer, Perplexity.ai, ChatGPT in cited prior work.
key_metrics: Answer accuracy (relaxed exact-match: prediction contains ground truth) on all four datasets; retrieval Precision and Recall (HotpotQA distractor setting); token utilization (input/output avg tokens per query) and reasoning-depth distribution for efficiency; cumulative Information Gain (IG, scored 1-10 by GPT-3.5-turbo) across DAG depth.
headline_result: On HotpotQA with Llama3.1-instruct-8B, Plan*RAG raises accuracy from 25.51 (Vanilla-RAG) to 31.12 and Plan*RAG SubQ reaches 40.44 vs ReAct 33.15; integrating Self-RAG (Plan*-Self-RAG) improves Self-RAG from 34.09 to 37.31 on HotpotQA (Llama2-13B). Consistent gains across HotpotQA/StrategyQA/MuSiQue/PopQA over RQ-RAG, Self-RAG, ReAct at comparable token cost.
ablations: (1) Base Plan*RAG (retrieve on original query) vs Plan*RAG SubQ (per-sub-query iterative retrieval): SubQ gives the largest gains and best precision. (2) Plan*-Self-RAG integration: adding Plan*RAG planning to Self-RAG improves it substantially on all datasets (e.g., StrategyQA 42.75->62.87 on Llama2-13B). (3) Reasoning-plan generator: fine-tuned Llama3.1-instruct-8B planner (LoRA, small HotpotQA-train subset) reaches 31.28 accuracy vs 31.97 for GPT-4o planner on the 1,300-sample HotpotQA-dev subset, showing the method does not depend on a powerful LLM planner. (4) Reasoning-DAG depth analysis: depth adapts to hop-count (PopQA mostly depth 0; HotpotQA mostly depth 2) while ReAct/QD-RAG over-shoot depth. (5) Retrieval effectiveness (HotpotQA distractor): Plan*RAGSubQ precision 27.43 / recall 36.57 / acc 31.27 vs ReAct 0.04 / 34.61 / 25.68 and QD-RAGSubQ 0.02 / 32.16 / 23.54. (6) Information Gain increases monotonically with DAG depth.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes (partially): intrinsic retrieval metrics (Precision, Recall on HotpotQA distractor, Table 4) and reasoning-process metrics (DAG depth distribution, Information Gain over depth) are reported separately from end-to-end answer accuracy (Tables 2-3).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: answer accuracy. Process: reasoning-DAG depth distribution vs ideal hop count, cumulative Information Gain across depth, and intermediate retrieval precision/recall - measuring reasoning-path and retrieval quality, not just final answers.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Plan*RAG maintains comparable input/output token cost to baselines (Fig. 4a, log avg tokens/query for ReAct/QD-RAG/CoT-RAG/Plan*RAG are similar) while improving accuracy. Same-depth DAG nodes execute in parallel, reducing latency from sequential sum (T_seq) to sum over depths of the max per-depth node time (T_Plan*RAG <= T_seq); per-node context is bounded (only parent answers + node documents) rather than growing linearly with reasoning steps. No dollar API-cost or wall-clock latency numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: top-5 documents retrieved per query/sub-query (Contriever-MS MARCO over 100-word Wikipedia chunks). Per-node context is bounded to the node's sub-query, its retrieved top-5 documents, and only its parent nodes' answers (constant per node, C_q^ours = |q| + |D_q| + sum over parents of (|p|+|G(p)|)), versus linearly growing context in sequential baselines.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (not a survey or benchmark paper).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing one). Dataset sizes used: HotpotQA dev-fullwiki 7,405 (plus a 1,300 dev subset for planner ablation), StrategyQA 2,234, MuSiQue-Ans 2,417, PopQA 1,399.
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020; REALM/Guu et al. 2020), Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022), query decomposition / least-to-most (Patel et al. 2022; Zhou et al. 2023), ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2023, used as a plug-in per-node solver), Contriever (Izacard et al. 2022). Conceptually related to Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al. 2024) and Reasoning-via-Planning (Hao et al. 2023) but uses a DAG external to the LM context.
contrasts_with: ReAct (reasoning chain kept inside the LM context, context overflow, sequential), CoT-RAG, Query Decomposition / QD-RAG, RQ-RAG (query rewriting/decomposition but sequential, in-context), RA-ISF, Self-RAG (self-reflection but still single-context implicit reasoning), C-RAG / contrastive-explanation RAG (Ranaldi et al. 2024). Plan*RAG's distinction: externalize the reasoning plan as a DAG outside the LM working memory, enabling atomic sub-queries, parallel execution, bounded context, and (future) backtracking.
lineage: Group C (RAG + planning). Sits in the line of structured/test-time-planning RAG for multi-hop QA: from CoT and query decomposition, through ReAct/Self-RAG/RQ-RAG (in-context iterative reasoning), to externalized-plan-as-DAG approaches; closely related to the authors' concurrent Plan×RAG (Planning-guided RAG, arXiv 2410.20753-adjacent) line and to later DAG/dependency-aware RAG search methods.
